newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says removes curbs on Bhutto's movements.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says removes curbs on Bhutto's movements.

text.p: Pakistan's new caretaker government said on Wednesday that it had removed all restrictions on ousted prime minister Benazir Bhutto's movements.

Information Minister Irshad Haqqani told a news conference that Bhutto, who was confined by police to her official residence after being sacked on Tuesday, "was free to carry out political activities and go wherever she likes".
"In the first 24 hours, certain restrictions were thought proper, but now she is absolutely free," Haqqani said.

He said Bhutto would be authorised to stay in the prime minister's official house for 10 days, but not be allowed to use the residence for party meetings or protests. "These restrictions apply only to the prime minister's house," Haqqani said.
Bhutto's defence minister, Aftab Shaaban Meerani, had filed a legal complaint on Tuesday claiming the ousted prime minister had been held "unlawfully incommunicado".
Lawyers for the caretaker government told a court on Wednesday that Bhutto was not under arrest, saying she was under police protection for her personal safety.
